arguments.summary: Independent risk view: both stocks have strong recent completed-session momentum, but the evidence supports a watch posture because policy/supply channels and elevated valuation sensitivity are material and not yet quantified.

claims.text: At the 2026-10-02 completed close, NVDA had outperformed SPY over 5, 21 and 63 sessions, while MU outperformed SPY over 21 and 63 sessions but lagged it over 5 sessions. These are backward-looking price-return comparisons, not forecasts.

MU’s annualized realized volatility was 49.55% over 21 sessions and 74.56% over 63 sessions, and its maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was 25.48%; NVDA’s corresponding realized volatilities were 24.85% and 38.25%, with a 10.58% maximum drawdown. The distinct windows and methodologies are descriptive only.

NVIDIA disclosed that export controls had effectively foreclosed it from China, that Chinese policies could impede any return, and that it depends on overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea. This establishes material policy and supply-chain risk channels but not a quantified current loss.

Micron disclosed that unresolved Section 232 and proposed Section 301 investigations could lead to tariffs or trade restrictions adverse to its business; its September 30 release also reported fiscal-2026 revenue of $133.19 billion and fiscal-Q1 2027 revenue guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion. Guidance is management’s forward-looking outlook, not an independently verified result.

The combination of strong price regimes and unquantified export/trade and supply risks makes near-term momentum an inadequate stand-alone basis for preferring either stock. MU’s higher realized volatility and deeper 63-session drawdown make its path-risk profile less forgiving than NVDA’s on the supplied data.

gaps.description: No market-derived valuation multiple, reconciled forward EPS, or corporate-action/share-basis bridge is supplied. Therefore neither a current valuation nor a valuation-based preference is established in this independent risk pass.

The dated advanced-computing rule and issuer disclosures do not quantify current revenue, margin, or supply impact for either issuer, and subsequent policy changes/applicability are not certified. This limits policy-impact sizing, not the disclosed existence of risk channels.

assumptions: Completed closes dated 2026-10-02, rather than stale single-venue snapshots, are the relevant market observations.
Historical realized volatility and price-regime statistics are descriptive risk context, not expected returns or calibrated probabilities.
Issuer guidance and risk disclosures are treated as dated company statements.
arguments.counter_thesis: Momentum could persist if AI-related demand and Micron’s guided revenue/margins continue to validate current operating strength while policy and supply channels do not worsen. The present evidence does not quantify enough to rank that possibility against the downside channels.

review_conditions.description: Reassess the risk view after the next issuer earnings disclosures and any verified export-control or tariff action; reduce the policy/supply concern only if updated disclosures quantify no material operational effect, and increase it if restrictions, licensing, customer access, or overseas supply are adversely affected.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both issuers disclose exposure to changing trade/export restrictions. The available evidence supports a common policy-risk channel, but not common revenue weights or a quantified correlation of outcomes.
shared_exposures.qualification: Dated coverage only; neither current applicability nor financial magnitude is established.

agent_report.work_summary: Reviewed the seeded completed-session price, comparative-return, technical-path, SEC-company-fact and filing-excerpt evidence to form an independent risk view; no new source inspection or valuation calculation was performed.
main_conclusions: Recent relative price strength does not eliminate risk; MU’s supplied historical path metrics were materially more volatile than NVDA’s.
NVIDIA has disclosed China-access and Taiwan/South Korea supply channels that can materially affect operations.
Micron’s strong reported/guided operating figures coexist with unresolved tariff and trade-risk channels.
Neither a current valuation nor a valuation-based preference can be supported from the supplied evidence alone.
agent_report.short_summary: Both names show positive medium-term price momentum, but policy/supply uncertainty makes momentum alone insufficient. MU carries the higher observed historical path risk in the supplied windows.
limitations: No current market-derived valuation multiple or forward-EPS reconciliation was supplied.
Policy documents and disclosures do not quantify present financial impact or certify subsequent rule changes.
No causal inference is drawn from ETF, macro, or price movements.
